claim: The FAQ says the maximum size of an individual file on S3 File Gateway is 5 TB, the maximum size of an individual object in S3. A file larger than 5 TB gets a "file too large" error and only the first 5 TB is uploaded.
question: What does the Storage Gateway FAQ give as the maximum size of an individual file on S3 File Gateway?

qualifiers.scope: individual file on S3 File Gateway
qualifiers.condition: the quota page states the same limit as 5 TiB; the S3 object maximum is now 50 TB

evidence.quote: The maximum size of an individual file is 5 TB, which is the maximum size of an individual object in S3. If you write a file larger than 5 TB, you will get a "file too large" error message and only the first 5 TB of the file will be uploaded.

note: d25-035. FAQ says 5 TB, the quota page says 5 TiB; the FAQ still calls it the S3 maximum although chapter 21 records s3-change-max-object-size-50-tb-2025-12.

claim: The FAQ says the minimum size and maximum size of a virtual tape you can create on a Tape Gateway is 100 GiB and 15 TiB, respectively.
question: How much data can one virtual tape hold on a Tape Gateway, according to the FAQ?

evidence.quote: The minimum size and maximum size of a virtual tape you can create on a Tape Gateway is 100 GiB and 15 TiB, respectively.

note: d25-035. Same values as the quota page.

claim: The FAQ says a single Tape Gateway can have up to 1,500 virtual tapes in the VTL with a maximum aggregate capacity of 1 PB, and there is no limit to the amount of data or number of virtual tapes you can archive.
question: How many virtual tapes can a Tape Gateway hold in its virtual tape library, and how many can you archive?

qualifiers.scope: virtual tapes in the VTL of one Tape Gateway
qualifiers.condition: archived tapes have no limit; the quota page gives 1 PiB

evidence.quote: A single Tape Gateway can have up to 1,500 virtual tapes in the VTL with a maximum aggregate capacity of 1 PB; however there is no limit to the amount of data or number of virtual tapes you can archive.

note: d25-033, d25-035. FAQ says 1 PB; the quota page says 1 PiB.

claim: The FAQ says each Volume Gateway can support up to 32 volumes. In cached mode each volume can be up to 32 TB, for a maximum of 1 PB per gateway; in stored mode each volume can be up to 16 TB, for a maximum of 512 TB per gateway.
question: How many volumes and how much volume data can one Volume Gateway manage, according to the FAQ?

qualifiers.condition: cached mode versus stored mode; the quota page states these in TiB and gives 1,024 TiB for cached volumes

evidence.quote: Each Volume Gateway can support up to 32 volumes. In cached mode, each volume can be up to 32 TB for a maximum of 1 PB of data per gateway (32 volumes, each 32 TB in size). In stored mode, each volume can be up to 16 TB for a maximum of 512 TB of data per gateway (32 volumes, each 16 TB in size).

note: d25-032, d25-035. Units differ from the quota page: FAQ uses TB and PB, quota page uses TiB (32 TiB, 16 TiB, 1,024 TiB, 512 TiB).

claim: With VMware high availability, a hardware, software or network failure makes VMware restart the gateway on a new host or on its existing host if that host is still operational, and users and applications experience up to 60 seconds of downtime during a restart.
question: How much downtime can users expect during a VMware HA restart of a Storage Gateway?

qualifiers.condition: gateway hosted on VMware with HA enabled

evidence.quote: During a hardware, software, or network failure, VMware will trigger a gateway restart on a new host or on its existing host if the host is still operational. At a maximum, users and applications will experience up to 60 seconds of downtime during a restart.
